     FairVLM: Enhancing Fairness and Prompt Sensitivity in Vision Language
                  Models for Medical Image Segmentation

         Md Motiur Rahman                  Saeka Rahman          Smriti Bhatt                           Miad Faezipour
                                                 Purdue University
                                           West Lafayette, IN 47907, USA
                            {rahma112, rahma122, bhatt32, mfaezipo}@purdue.edu


                        Abstract

Vision-language models (VLMs) have demonstrated sub-
stantial promise in medical image segmentation by utiliz-
ing radiology reports as prompts to segment regions of in-
terest. However, VLM deployment in clinical settings is
challenged by two intertwined issues: i) demographic bias,
where performance varies across demographic groups, and
ii) prompt sensitivity, where semantically similar prompts
yield inconsistent outputs. These challenges are intercon-
nected; demographic underrepresentation can worsen a
model’s sensitivity to prompts, and prompt instability can
more heavily affect certain demographic groups. In this
study, we present FairVLM, a unified framework that ad-
dresses both demographic disparity and prompt sensitiv-               Figure 1. Demonstration of how a state-of-the-art vision-language
ity in VLMs. FairVLM integrates three key components:                 model (VLM), SAMed [41] (on the left), exhibits performance
(1) Semantic-Retaining Counterfactual Prompting (SRCP),               bias across demographic attributes (e.g., race, ethnicity); varying
which generates clinically consistent and diverse prompt              levels of sample representation, categorized as high representation
variations via large language models; (2) Demographic-                (HR), medium representation (MR), and low representation (LR)
Aware Feature Normalization (DAFN), a lightweight mod-                groups based on the relative frequency of samples in the training
ule that mitigates latent representation bias across demo-            dataset; and prompt variability. FairVLM (on the right) effectively
graphic groups; and (3) a Fairness-Calibrated Loss (FCL)              mitigates these biases by ensuring equitable performance across
that explicitly penalizes performance disparities while en-           underrepresented groups and diverse textual descriptions.
couraging prompt consistency. Extensive evaluations on                guage prompts to identify anatomical structures. Their flex-
the Harvard-FairSeg dataset show that FairVLM signifi-                ibility fits well with clinical practice, where diagnostic re-
cantly improves equity-scaled segmentation. It also re-               ports differ among practitioners and institutions [32, 33,
duces demographic disparity (DI) by over 65% and rel-                 41]. However, the deployment of VLMs in clinical en-
ative performance gap (RPG) by over 60%, while main-                  vironments is hindered by two interrelated challenges: (i)
taining or boosting overall accuracy. FairVLM is robust               demographic bias leading to performance gaps across de-
to prompt changes, with less than 0.5% performance drop               mographic groups [20, 31, 40], and (ii) prompt sensitiv-
across varied prompts, and also generalizes well on unseen            ity, where semantically similar prompts lead to inconsistent
datasets. These findings present FairVLM as a new state-of-           predictions [5, 26, 28]. These issues are especially criti-
the-art, robust, and adaptable framework for a fair, prompt-          cal in high-stakes clinical environments, where biased or
invariant vision-language model. Code and data are avail-             inconsistent results can cause misdiagnosis, delayed care,
able at https://github.com/Rahman-Motiur/FairVLM.                     or unequal treatment [31, 32].

valid and semantically coherent counterfactual prompts, which we score, rank, and select the top k = 3 relevant prompts for linguistic
variability. The DAFN module reduces bias in the learned multimodal representations by normalizing feature statistics across demographic
groups, while the FCL module penalizes performance disparities, encouraging equitable segmentation across underrepresented groups.

dress this, we propose Demographic-Aware Feature Nor-                                                                                                                                                     Calibrated Loss (FCL), a fairness-aware regularization,
malization (DAFN), a simple yet effective technique that                                                                                                                                                  which aims to minimize performance disparities across
improves demographic invariance by normalizing features                                                                                                                                                   groups while preserving task accuracy. Specifically, it
with respect to group-specific statistics. DAFN encourages                                                                                                                                                shares motivation with prior fairness-aware loss formula-

ity, or language.                                                                                                                                                                                         weighting as in [11].

clearly demonstrate that each component of FairVLM con-                                                      framework for medical vision-language segmentation that
